links.note: In 1943 the Russian and Georgian churches restored communion with each other, a modern study says. It ties the step to Stalin's change of church policy that year.

links.note: The patriarch of Constantinople, Demetrios I, gave the Georgian church a tomos. That is a formal church decree. A modern study says it made the church's self-rule legal. Other Orthodox churches had already accepted it in practice since 1943.
